messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend the existing game to make the world feel more alive and immersive while preserving the current playable horror experience.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game change now without asking clarifying questions.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at the end of the work.
- Keep the game playable and in the same overall style as the existing town exploration horror game.
- Add a more living world through ambient life and dynamic character activity.
- Use screenshots only for validation when needed; no further action required here.

## Decisions
- The world should feel more alive by adding ambient critters and giving townspeople simple daily routines and idle activity instead of static stand-ins.
- This was implemented as a lightweight expansion inside the existing raycast town scene without changing the core storytelling gameplay structure.
- The existing horror tone, UI, map, and objective flow were preserved.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a small set of ambient creatures to the world: a stray cat and several crows.
- Updated NPC data to include activity state, timers, motion, and look/gesture behavior.
- Updated sprite rendering to draw the new critters as visible world entities.
- Expanded NPC movement logic so people appear to have routine-based movement and idle activity rather than being fully static.
- Adjusted dialogue text to briefly mention the residents’ present activity.
- Added a few minor world-liveliness details to the movement and animation systems.
- Ran project checks as available in the workspace.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review the current game behavior in-browser and verify the living-world additions feel coherent and not visually broken.
2. If the game still feels too static or the new activity breaks the original mood, tune the NPC routines and creature behaviors.
3. Finalize any brief notes on assumptions and the resulting living-world changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: core gameplay, NPC logic, raycast rendering, and the living-world additions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game shell and HUD layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: visual styling for the game UI and overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: project overview and project metadata.

## Important Context
- The game is an existing first-person horror town exploration prototype that was extended rather than rebuilt.
- The requested “make the world more living” change was implemented by adding ambient life and more active NPC behavior while keeping the same game structure and narrative.
- No unresolved user ask remains; the task was completed in the current working tree.

## Objective
- Make the existing horror town game feel more alive while preserving its style, story flow, UI, and playable experience.

## Requirements
- Add ambient life and dynamic character activity.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Add a stray cat and crows, and give residents simple routines and idle movement within the existing raycast scene.
- Keep the horror tone and core story structure intact.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cat and crow entities with custom rendering and ambient movement.
- Added NPC activity states, routine-based movement, gestures, and activity-aware dialogue.
- Added an “Ask about today” dialogue option and response; moved its handling to an early return so it works across residents.
- Earlier `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed, before the latest dialogue edit.

### Active
- Run syntax and diff checks after the latest edit.
- Review the game in-browser and tune movement or rendering if needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Continue browser review; a local server was started on port 3002, but the game has not yet been opened or visually checked.
3. Preserve the unrelated `Agents.md` change while reviewing final status.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: NPC routines, critter behavior, rendering, and dialogue changes.
- `Agents.md`: Has an unrelated removal of seven mobile-browser-game guidance lines; do not treat as part of the game feature.

- Changes are uncommitted. `git status --short` showed `Agents.md` and `game.js` modified.
- A previous diff check found trailing whitespace in `game.js`; that whitespace was removed and the subsequent check passed before the latest dialogue edit.
